title: OML record
description: One misconception in the Open Misconception Library. Schema version 0.1.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor support.

id.description: Stable, human-readable ID. Lowercase, dot-separated; the first segment is the domain. Never reused.

uuid.description: Opaque identifier, unique across the library. Used as the CASE CFItem identifier.

version.description: Semantic version of this record's content. Bump patch for wording, minor for added evidence, major for a changed statement.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `reviewed` requires a `review` block; `merged` requires `history.merged_into`.

title.description: Short label for the misconception, a noun phrase.

statement.description: The belief, stated as the learner would hold it. A belief, not a wrong answer.

kind.description: Mechanism by which the belief arises.

domain.description: Subject area, matching the first segment of `id` (e.g. `math`, `prog`). May be qualified (`math.fractions`).

about.description: Concepts this misconception is about. Strings are either OML concept IDs or CASE item URIs; which is canonical is an open decision (b).

level_band.description: Education levels where the misconception is typically observed.

locale.description: BCP 47 tag for the language of `statement` and examples. Default `en`.

evidence_patterns.description: Observable response patterns that indicate the belief. At least one, each with a concrete example.

discriminators.description: How to tell this misconception apart from a slip and from its nearest neighbours.

vs_slip.description: What distinguishes a systematic holder of this belief from someone who made a one-off error.

vs.description: Keyed by neighbouring OML id; value explains the observable difference.

relations.description: Typed links to other records or external nodes. Open object in v0.1; keys beyond those listed are rejected by the validator. `conflicts_with` and `resolved_by` mirror the Knowledge Map's `conflicts-with` and `resolves` edges. The four provisional keys are misconception-to-misconception edges pending open decision (a).

resolved_by.description: Concepts whose understanding corrects this belief.

confusable_with.description: Misconceptions that produce similar evidence and need a discriminator.

specializes.description: A more general misconception of which this is a special case.

co_occurs_with.description: Misconceptions frequently held by the same learners.

blocked_by.description: Misconceptions that must be resolved before this one can be addressed.

alignments.description: Links to items in external schemes (CASE frameworks, other inventories).

provenance.description: Where this record's claim comes from.

origin.description: How the record entered OML. `llm-drafted` records must cite literature in `sources` and stay `draft` until reviewed.

prevalence.description: Reserved for measured prevalence. Out of scope for v1; shape is provisional.

review.description: Present when status is `reviewed`. Records who checked the record and when.

merged_into.description: Required when status is `merged`. The surviving record.

license.description: Licence for this record's content. All OML records are CC BY 4.0.

item_shape.description: The kind of task on which the pattern shows (e.g. `add two fractions with unlike denominators`).

signature.description: The response rule a holder of the belief follows, stated so a grader could apply it.

item.description: The task as shown to the learner.

response.description: The response a holder of the belief gives.

external.description: A URI or identifier outside OML (a CASE item, a Knowledge Map node).

relation.description: How this record relates to the aligned item. Default `about`.

identifier.description: The source's own identifier for this misconception, if any.

license.description: Licence of the source, if text was reused.
